title: Lt. Col. Thomas Jordan to 'My Dearest Rachel' (Rose Greenhow), 1861: the cipher original (NARA naId 6925618, catalogue 646) and the clerk's clear copy (naId 1634051, catalogue 645), with the 1864 Greenhow key

steps.what: Fetched NARA naId 1634051 (6 images), naId 6925618 (1 image) and M1091 naId 62017285 images 0483-0485; the files were fetched a second time for the check and are byte-identical.

Identified naId 1634051 images 1-2 as a clerk's clear copy of Jordan's letter to 'My Dearest Rachel', and naId 6925618 as the cipher original of the same letter: every clear phrase of the fragment occurs in the copy, in the same order. Images 3-6 of 1634051 are a different clear letter and an envelope to Miss Gertrude L. Greenhow docketed 'Capt Moore of the Union 29 Apl 1861'.
Transcribed the cipher groups of the photostat on inverted crops, twice independently: 22 groups, 89 signs, 7 uncertain.

Applied the 1864 Greenhow key (M1091 image 0484) unchanged: all 82 securely read signs give the clear copy's letter at that place (HAR, SCOTT, HANS FIELD FORTIFICATION, OULDER, LIE, ANY, CANG, BOO, LIEU, COLONEL, IN ...). Image 0483 does not apply.

decode.py: 20,000 random keys mean 3.1/82, best 36/82; key shifted 1, 2, 3, 13: 0/82; groups assigned to the wrong copy words: mean 5.5, best 19; whole groups right: 22/22 against a random-key best of 4/22.

One web search (Jordan, 'Dearest Rachel', Greenhow, Hardee's Tactics, shoulder straps) found catalogue and overview pages only (NARA, SNAC, Wikipedia, whitehousehistory.org, dh.scu.edu); no printed text of the letter.

Review (Claude, for Daniel Bourdeau), print step: grepped the archive.org texts of the Official Records Ser. II vol. 2 (warofrebellion02unit_0; the Greenhow case papers, pp. 561-577), Pinkerton's Spy of the Rebellion (1883; Gutenberg 34973) and Greenhow's My Imprisonment (1863) for 'Rachel', 'Hardee', 'flannel', 'shoulder straps' and 'cipher'. None prints this letter. OR II 2 pp. 564-565 prints Jordan's letter to Benjamin of 29 Oct 1861: he arranged the cipher 'last April', used the alias Thomas John Rayford, and thought the War Department, holding one of her letters in it, 'ought to have worked out the key'. Fishel (1996) and Blackman (2005) are lending-library copies on archive.org; their full text could not be searched, and web searches found no transcription in either.

Review (Claude, for Daniel Bourdeau): outcome method changed from 'read after matching with key from external sources' to 'read from existing decipherment'. The clerk's clear copy (naId 1634051 images 1-2) gives every cipher passage in plain words, so the text was not obtained by the key; matching the signs to the 1864 key is what the project added. Reading re-read against decryption.txt, the clear copy and the photostat: grade B.

outcome.method_basis: A complete decipherment existed: the clerk's clear copy of the letter (NARA naId 1634051 images 1-2) gives every cipher passage of naId 6925618 in plain words, and an interlinear gloss 'h a r' deciphers the first group on the original. The project's contribution is the sign match: the 1864 key found on Greenhow's body (M1091 naId 62017285 image 0484) gives the copy's letter for all 82 securely read signs, unchanged, and the two NARA items were identified as one letter.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py: 82 of 89 transcribed signs read securely, all agreeing with the clear copy; the unread groups L12, C1 and R5 are not counted in the 89.
outcome.notes: No new plaintext: the clear copy already gives these passages. What is added: the two NARA items identified as one letter (catalogue 645 and 646), the correct correspondents of 646, and the proof that the 1864 key reads the 1861 cipher unchanged. The torn passages of the copy are lost on the original too.

texts.label: Jordan to 'My Dearest Rachel', 1861: cipher original naId 6925618

reading_review.note: Read reading.md against decryption.txt, the clear copy and the photostat. Every cipher group gives the copy's word (HAR, SCOTT, HANS FIELD FORTIFICATION, LIEU, COLONEL ...), so the decipherment is sound; but on the fragment itself most sentences are torn and complete only with the copy's words in brackets, which is why _check_reading.py flags 8 of 13 sentences. Coherent, but not with scattered holes: grade B. Replaces the contributor's own grade A (WAINUT agent).

texts.summary: Thomas Jordan, newly a lieutenant colonel, asks 'Rachel' (Rose Greenhow) to get him Hardee's and Scott's Tactics, Mahan's Field Fortification, 8 yards of navy-blue flannel and shoulder straps for his rank, to be sent by hand; the clear copy adds that he feared an earlier letter had failed to reach her: he had then no access to his cipher, and a letter in ordinary characters 'was intercepted' (the copy has gaps here). Domestic in content, but it shows the Jordan-Greenhow cipher in use in 1861 with the same key as in 1864.

prior.where: The clear copy NARA naId 1634051 images 1-2 (filed in the same series) gives every cipher passage in plain words; an interlinear gloss 'h a r' sits under the first cipher group of naId 6925618. No printed transcription found: the Official Records Ser. II vol. 2 (Greenhow case, pp. 561-577), Pinkerton (1883) and Greenhow (1863) do not print it; Fishel (1996) and Blackman (2005) checked by web search only.

human: Outside contribution (WAINUT): the operator chose the catalogue items; transcription, key application, controls and the identification of the two NARA items as one letter were done by AI language-model agents and checked against the images. No hand correction of readings recorded.
